objectives: Name the three parts of a story.
Tell the characters in the story of Pip.
Use the new words for a lost puppy.
Follow the steps Pip took to get home.
Say the small lesson of the story out loud.
Retell the story to someone else in your own words.

sections.body:
This is a story about Pip. Pip is a small brown puppy with one white paw.

Pip lives with his family in a little house at the end of a lane. His family loves him very much. They play with him in the garden. They let him sleep on a soft blanket by the door.

Every good story has three parts. It has a beginning, a middle and an end. The beginning tells you who the story is about. The middle is where something goes wrong. The end is where everything comes right again.

Pip's story starts on a wet afternoon. The back gate was open. Pip slipped out into the rain. He did not know the way home.

You will meet a few friends along the way. There is Mop the cat, who likes to sit on warm walls. There is an old woman with a basket of bread. There is also a smell of rain on hot stones, and a sound that Pip knows very well.

This story is a little sad in the middle. That is okay. Stories are like that. The good part comes at the end, when Pip finds his own front door and his own family waiting on the step.
examples: This is the beginning of Pip's story.
The middle is the part where Pip gets lost.
The end is the part where Pip comes home.
sections.heading: A little puppy who lost his way

sections.body:
The sun was hiding behind a grey sky that day. Mum opened the back door to hang out the washing.

Pip was asleep on the blanket. He woke up. He saw the open door. He saw the bright green garden. He thought of a bird.

Pip ran out through the gate. He ran past the washing line. He ran down the lane, faster and faster, with the rain starting to fall on his nose.

Then Pip stopped. The lane looked much bigger than before. The houses were grey shapes in the rain. His family was nowhere to be seen.

Pip did not know what to do. He pulled his little tail. He made a small sound, like "awooo", and nobody answered.

This is the part of the story where you hold your breath. Pip is alone, and he is wet, and he is very far from home.
examples: Pip slipped out through the open gate.
The rain fell on his nose.
Pip was alone and he did not know the way home.
sections.heading: The afternoon Pip went missing

sections.body:
Pip began to walk. He walked along the lane until it turned into a street.

On a warm wall sat Mop the cat. Mop opened one eye.

"You are a long way from home," said Mop.

"How do you know?" said Pip.

"Because I have seen you every afternoon for two years," said Mop. "You come out of that lane with a bird in your mouth. You always come back the same way."

So Pip turned around and looked. The lane was behind him, long and grey. But it was still there. That was a good thing to know.

Pip kept walking. The rain got heavier. He came to a little bakery with warm windows. The old woman with the basket of bread saw him.

"You are shaking," she said. "Come under my awning for a moment."

She gave him a piece of bread and a warm cloth for his white paw. Then she pointed down the road.

"Go that way," she said. "I can hear the church bell. That bell is near your house."

Pip listened. Far away, over the roofs, there was a sound. It was a small sound. But Pip had heard it every Sunday of his life. It was the bell.
examples: You are a long way from home, said Mop the cat.
Come under my awning for a moment.
I can hear the church bell. It is near your house.
sections.heading: The long walk Pip took

sections.body:
Pip did not know the way. But he did know three things, and they were enough.

Here is what he did, in order. You can use these steps any time you feel lost.
examples: Stop, stand still and look around you.
I know this smell. It comes from our kitchen.
Which way is the bell, please?
sections.heading: How Pip found his way home
steps: Stop and stand still. Look around you and breathe.
Think of one thing you know well. A sound, a smell, a tree.
Ask a friendly grown-up or animal for one small direction.
Walk slowly towards the thing you know. Look for more of it.
Look for one more clue. Follow the clue, not just the road.
When you see a gate you know, go to it and call out loud.

sections.body:
These are the new words in this story. Read them once, then read the story again and find them.

A **lost** puppy is one that cannot find the way home. It is not a bad word. It just means the puppy needs help.

A **scent** is a smell that stays in the air for a while. Every place has its own scent, and animals can follow it for miles.

A **collar** is the band a dog wears around its neck. It can hold a name tag, so a lost dog can be brought back to its family.

A **den** is a small safe place where a dog likes to rest. Pip's den was the warm blanket by the door.
sections.heading: The words in Pip's story

terms.example: Pip was lost, but he was not frightened of the dark.
terms.gloss: Not able to find the way home. If you are lost, you are not in trouble. You just need help.

terms.example: Pip knew the scent of his own garden.
terms.gloss: A smell that hangs in the air. Dogs can smell scents and follow them a long way.

terms.example: Mum put Pip's name on his new collar.
terms.gloss: The band that goes around a dog's neck. It can hold a small tag with the dog's name.

terms.example: Pip's den was a soft blanket by the door.
terms.gloss: A small quiet place where a dog feels safe and can sleep.

sections.body:
Pip got home, and his family was waiting on the step with a warm towel and a big hug.

The lesson in this story is small, and it is worth keeping. Home is not only a building. Home is also the smell of your own kitchen, the sound of a bell you know, and the way your family sounds when they are glad to see you.

If you are ever lost, you do not have to be brave and silent. Stand still, find one thing you know, and ask someone friendly for one small direction. Mop the cat was right. The way home was still there. It was just waiting for Pip to look.
examples: Home is where your family is glad to see you.
If you are lost, find one thing you know and start there.
Ask a friendly grown-up for one small direction.
sections.heading: What Pip learned

item.summary: Pip slips out of the gate and loses his way in the rain. Follow him from the first wet paw to the last step home. You will learn the three parts of a story, the words Pip's story uses, and the little trick that helped him find his own front door.
item.title: The Lost Puppy Finds His Way Home
